name: Democracy
summary: Democracy holds that political authority rests on the people, who rule themselves as political equals, usually by electing representatives in free and periodic elections. Its mainstream, liberal form pairs majority rule with civil liberties, equality before the law and constitutional protection of minorities. It is a view about who should hold power and how, and takes few positions on economic, social or foreign policy.
scope: The mainstream modern ideal of representative, liberal democracy as set out in John Stuart Mill's Considerations on Representative Government, the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (Article 21) and the Stanford Encyclopedia's account of democratic theory. It treats democracy as a political ideal, not a bundle of economic or cultural policies, so most statements outside government and rights are answered neutral with low confidence. It excludes democratic socialism and social democracy, which have their own profiles.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Inferred from liberal democracy's protection of freedom of religion and association, which tells against state control of churches (Article 18 of the UDHR).

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Democracies include ceremonial monarchs and presidents, and partisan elected presidents; the democratic ideal does not decide the matter.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Democratic theory is split between the self-determination of peoples and majority rule within existing borders, and gives no settled answer.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Democracy permits federal and autonomous arrangements but does not require them; it takes no side.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Democracy holds that authority comes from the people, not from divine descent; the UDHR says the will of the people is the basis of government.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Democracy takes no position on tax design; the electorate chooses.

character-from-environment.rationale: Democratic theory does not address nature versus nurture, though political equality sits more easily with the environmental view (Mill stressed education).

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Constitutional democracy requires rulers to be bound by law and accountable; the UDHR rests human rights on the rule of law.

space-expansion.rationale: Unrelated to democracy; it takes no position on civilizational goals.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Mixed government is an older theory that modern democrats often see as embodied in checks and balances; Mill also favoured representation tempered by safeguards, but adherents are divided.

leader-cult.rationale: Democratic equality and accountability cut against glorifying leaders as embodiments of the nation; Mill warned against concentrating adulation and power in one person.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law is outside democratic theory; democracies legislate it differently.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Democracy is a method of collective decision-making and takes no side on this question; its adherents differ, so it is left neutral.

land-redistribution.rationale: Democracy is a method of collective decision-making and takes no side on this question; its adherents differ, so it is left neutral.

refugee-return.rationale: Democracy is a method of collective decision-making and takes no side on this question; its adherents differ, so it is left neutral.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Inferred from democratic self-determination by the governed in the Universal Declaration, which grounds authority in the people living under a government, not in nationality abroad.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Article 18 of the Universal Declaration protects the freedom to change one's religion, which democratic rights frameworks treat as non-negotiable.

women-must-cover.rationale: The Universal Declaration protects equality, religion and expression as personal freedoms, which a legal dress mandate for women contradicts.

common-currency.rationale: Democracy is a method of collective decision-making and takes no side on this question; its adherents differ, so it is left neutral.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Democracy is a method of collective decision-making and takes no side on this question; its adherents differ, so it is left neutral.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Democracy is a method of collective decision-making and takes no side on this question; its adherents differ, so it is left neutral.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Inferred from the Universal Declaration's equality before the law, which makes equal rights where one lives the democratic remedy for persecution.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Democracy is a method of collective decision-making and takes no side on this question; its adherents differ, so it is left neutral.

ban-cartels.rationale: Democracy is a method of collective decision-making and takes no side on this question; its adherents differ, so it is left neutral.

no-bailouts.rationale: Democracy is a method of collective decision-making and takes no side on this question; its adherents differ, so it is left neutral.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Mainstream liberal democracy pairs majority rule with constitutional protection of minorities, so it does not put majorities above courts and rights.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Democracy is a method of collective decision-making and takes no side on this question; its adherents differ, so it is left neutral.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Democracy is a method of collective decision-making and takes no side on this question; its adherents differ, so it is left neutral.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Democracy is a method of collective decision-making and takes no side on this question; its adherents differ, so it is left neutral.

moral-incentives.rationale: Democracy is a method of collective decision-making and takes no side on this question; its adherents differ, so it is left neutral.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Democracy holds that authority rests on the will of the people expressed in elections, not on a self-appointed armed vanguard.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The Universal Declaration bars distinctions of birth and status, and Mill defends political equality against rule by inherited rank.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Democracy as a method of rule takes no position on how history is taught.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Mill defended temporary despotism over less advanced peoples while the UDHR affirms self-government for all; the ideal itself is split.

patriotic-education.rationale: Democracy takes no position on patriotic education; adherents differ.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Democracy takes no side on race-conscious preferences.

public-money-creation.rationale: Democracy as a political ideal takes no side on who creates money.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Democracy takes no side on economic theory.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Democracy takes no side on influence in former imperial lands.

delink-world-market.rationale: Democracy takes no side on development strategy.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Democracy takes no side on class analysis of global inequality.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The UDHR guarantees equal protection against discrimination, which liberal democracy generally upholds; inferred.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Liberal democracy pairs majority rule with constitutional protection of rights and minorities.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Democracy is a method of rule and takes no side on colonial treaties; self-determination arguments cut both ways.

elective-rulers.rationale: Authority resting on the will of the people (UDHR Art. 21) and Mill's case against hereditary rule imply elected rulers, though ceremonial monarchs are compatible.

minority-veto.rationale: Majority rule with minority protections is the mainstream view; a veto for each member would let any member block the majority.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred from the principle that authority rests on the people's consent and the rule of law.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Democracy backs elected lawmaking but also constitutional limits and judicial review, so it does not settle the question.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Democracy takes no position on animal ethics.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Democracy takes no position on the use of animals.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Democracy takes no position on duties of the wealthy.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Mill and democratic theory treat active citizenship as valuable and as a safeguard of self-rule.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Democracy takes no position on mass culture and the media.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Democracy takes no position on how ruling classes hold power.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Democracy takes no position on world-economy structure.

native-born-offices.rationale: Political equality and UDHR Art. 21's equal access to public service imply naturalized citizens may hold office.

party-own-road.rationale: Democracy takes no position on communist party independence.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Democracy takes no position on development strategy.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Democracy takes no position on reopening borders; self-determination arguments cut both ways.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Political equality means leadership is open to all citizens whatever their ancestry.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Democratic adherents split between militant-democracy constitutions that bar fascism and neutral ones, and the ideology is silent on it.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Democracy takes no position on comparing fascism and communism, though it opposes both.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Democracy takes no position on historical questions.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Democracy takes no position on monuments.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Democracy takes no position on male disadvantage programmes.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Democracy takes no position on domestic violence services.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The UDHR frames democratic rights as universal, though scholars debate local forms; inferred.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Democracy requires civilian control, with authority resting on the people's will (UDHR Art. 21), not an army guardian.

paid-care-work.rationale: Democracy takes no position on paying care work.

filial-duty.rationale: Democracy as a political ideal is silent on family duties between generations; nothing is inferred beyond neutrality.

office-by-exam.rationale: Mill favours competitive examination for administrative posts but insists the governing body be elected, so a democrat generally rejects exams in place of election for political office.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Democratic theory takes no stand on foreign ownership; democrats divide on economic nationalism.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from the liberal-democratic emphasis on individual liberty (Mill), though democracy as such does not address divorce law.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Mill argues representatives should use their own judgment and not be bound by pledges, favouring regular elections over binding instruction, though direct-democracy strands differ.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: A question of economic policy on which democrats of all kinds disagree; the ideal itself is silent.

land-use-tenure.rationale: UDHR Article 17 affirms the right to own property, so mainstream liberal democracy is inferred to reject communal use-only land tenure.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Mill holds that the representative assembly's core function is to control the government, including voting taxes and supply; legislative control of the purse is a standard democratic principle.

single-official-language.rationale: Mill thought free institutions work best within one nationality, but liberal democracies also protect minority language rights; democrats are split.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from UDHR's property and non-discrimination principles; democracy as such does not address the issue.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: UDHR bars discrimination and promotes equality before the law, but democrats are split on whether discrimination is judged by intent or outcome.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Democracy as a political ideal takes no position on consumer culture.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from the UDHR's emphasis on rights and peace and democratic self-determination; democrats nonetheless have often backed insurgents against dictatorships.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Self-rule by peoples is central to democracy, so forcible intervention to stop an ally changing its alliance or system is inferred to be rejected.

missingStatements.text: Legislative seats should be allocated to parties in proportion to the votes they receive.
missingStatements.rationale: Mill argues that true democracy represents minorities in proportion to their numbers, and the Stanford entry compares proportional with single-member systems, though democrats differ on the electoral system.

notes: Democracy is treated as a political method. Democratic socialists, liberals and populists who call themselves democrats answer many economic and social statements differently, which is why most of those answers are neutral and low confidence.
